REVISEThe exclusive-strip compensation lemma, the weighted bipartite cut formula, and the relaxed-model optimality statement are correct under the granted dependencies. The submitted all- $p$  geometric proof needs revision: its claimed endpoint separation is false. This leaves a specific support-compatibility check unproved, rather than establishing that the proposed family is infeasible.The intended negative-flux phenomenon survives a small coordinate repair described below. The componentwise direction comparison is also correct and is strictly stronger than the best single global direction in the alternating family for every  $k\ge2$ .I reviewed    adaptive-strip-compensation-review.txt, including its appended dependency. Section and line references below refer to that attachment. This is a written mathematical review; the reported finite controls and Lean declarations are not premises for the geometric conclusions.1. The strengthened per-strip tip count is validThe conclusion
$$L_i=2b_i-2$$
is justified, although I recommend replacing the compressed argument in §1, lines 26–31, with an argument that explicitly uses the granted global conservation law.Represent each parallel mouth in its physical band by a nonempty interval of physical tiles,
$$I_s=[\ell_s,r_s],$$
with its two parallel terminal-tip positions immediately outside it, at  $\ell_s-1$  and  $r_s+1$ . Let  $J_i$  be a coalesced strip containing  $b_i$  member mouths.First, every parallel tip counted inside  $J_i$  belongs to a mouth in this same coalesced strip. Its own mouth meets or is adjacent to  $J_i$ , so the coalescing rule includes it.Second, at least two of the  $2b_i$  member tip occurrences lie outside  $J_i$ : the left tip of a mouth attaining the minimum left endpoint, and the right tip of a mouth attaining the maximum right endpoint. Consequently,
$$L_i\le 2b_i-2.$$
The granted global identity now gives
$$\sum_i L_i=2B-2C=\sum_i(2b_i-2).$$
Thus the nonnegative quantities  $2b_i-2-L_i$  sum to zero, and each is zero.This proves the per-strip formula without needing to leave “the  $2b_i$  distinct parallel tip tiles” as an additional implicit geometric assertion. Opposite allowed source orientations do not affect this interval argument. Perpendicular tips remain in the separate phase term.It follows correctly that
$$D_i=2b_i+f_i+a_i+d'_i$$
and hence
$$D_i\ge \max(0,2b_i+f_i)=q_i.$$
Finding: accept the strengthened identity, with the proof clarification above.2. The general compensation lemma spends physical resources correctlyFor an independent set  $I$  in the graph defined by all physical strip intersections, the selected strips have pairwise disjoint physical tile sets. Therefore their actual no- $P$  deficits satisfy
$$\sum_{i\in I}D_i\le D_G.$$
Combining this with the strip bounds and the granted ledger gives
$$\Delta=-B+D_G+R
   \ge -B+\sum_{i\in I}D_i+R
   \ge q(I)-B+R.$$
This is the asserted lemma.The accounting is sound:A no- $P$  tile with deficit two is used once, with its actual weight two.Source tips, comb ends, shifted squares and matching exports are not separately added as donors.The remainder  $R$  occurs once.The selected strips may compensate the charges of sources whose own strips were not selected. The whole-receiver ledger permits that aggregate compensation.Thus  $q(I)\ge B$  proves the coefficient-one inequality
$$|T_0|+|M_0|\le \frac{mn}{2}$$
through the stated physical ledger.The optional edge-deletion sentence at lines 45–47 needs one qualification: for a certificate intended to hold uniformly over a class of completions, the shared donor deficit must vanish throughout that class. A zero observed in one baseline justifies deletion for that baseline only. The main graph retains all intersections, so this qualification does not affect the submitted lemma or star construction.3. The cut formula and relaxed-model optimum are exactWeighted independent setsPut  $Q=\sum_i q_i$ . The network in §3 has the correct capacities:
$$c(s,i)=q_i,\qquad c(j,t)=q_j,\qquad c(i,j)=Q+1$$
for horizontal vertices  $i$ , vertical vertices  $j$ , and graph edges  $ij$ .A cut of capacity at most  $Q$  exists, so a minimum cut cannot cross an arc of capacity  $Q+1$ . Its horizontal sink-side vertices and vertical source-side vertices therefore form a vertex cover. Conversely, every vertex cover produces a cut of exactly its weight. Taking complements proves
$$W=Q-\operatorname{mincut}.$$
Zero weights, isolated vertices and  $Q=0$  cause no problem. This is an ordinary application of classical integral max-flow/min-cut, appropriately presented without a new-flow-theorem claim.Relaxed resource modelThe relaxation can be written explicitly as
$$\begin{aligned}
\min\quad &\sum_{e\in E(H)}x_e+\sum_{i\in V(H)}y_i,\\
\text{subject to}\quad&
y_i+\sum_{e\ni i}x_e\ge q_i,\\
&x_e,y_i\ge0.
\end{aligned}$$
Here  $x_e$  is shared edge resource and  $y_i$  is private resource.For every independent set  $I$ , summing its constraints counts any edge resource at most once. Hence every feasible assignment costs at least  $q(I)$ , and therefore at least  $W$ .For a maximum flow of value  $v$ , set
$$x_{ij}=f_{ij},\qquad
y_i=q_i-\sum_{e\ni i}f_e.$$
The terminal capacities ensure  $y_i\ge0$ . Every vertex receives exactly its demand, and the total cost is
$$v+(Q-2v)=Q-v=W.$$
This proves the claimed optimum. It also proves that the real-valued relaxation has an integral optimum when the  $q_i$  are integral.The interpretation of  $W<B$  is properly limited: those scalar demands and that relaxed incidence model cannot, by themselves, force total resource at least  $B$ . Physical capacities, feasible donor locations, phase gains, shifted deficits and  $R$  can still provide additional information.Exact computational certificates need a flow witnessThere is a small distinction worth making explicit in lines 93–96. Checking an independent set, a cover and their weights verifies the resulting lower bound. A cut and its complementary independent set alone do not prove that the cut is minimum.For a solver-independent certificate of the claimed exact optimum, also provide a feasible flow whose value equals the cut capacity. Local capacity and conservation checks then certify optimality.For the star family this is particularly simple: its center has weight two, so the center alone is a cover of weight two. Sending one unit through each of two leaf-center edges gives a feasible flow of value two. These witnesses establish the optimum directly.4. The concrete error in the original all- $p$  geometryThe endpoint distance is three, not fourSection 4, lines 158–164, claims that distinct  $H_i$  endpoint sets have Manhattan distance at least four. With the stated chamber origins, write
$$R_i=2+4i.$$
The two chamber rows of  $H_i$  are  $R_i,R_i+1$ ; the next chamber begins at  $R_i+4$ . Their column intervals overlap.For any common chamber column  $z$ ,
$$(R_i+1,z)\in P(H_i),\qquad
(R_i+4,z)\in P(H_{i+1}),$$
and their distance is exactly three. For example, the first two chambers contain
$$(3,7)\quad\text{and}\quad(6,7).$$
This is a demonstrated error in the written proof.Distance three suffices to prevent endpoint-component joining and to prevent a one-step support from seeing a foreign endpoint. It does not suffice to prevent adjacency between two supports: the vertices
$$(R_i+2,z),\qquad(R_i+3,z)$$
would be adjacent if both were selected. Each would then have its own endpoint neighbor and an additional selected neighbor, violating feasibility.The missing condition is preciseLet  $T(H_i)$  denote the prescribed support set of the individual source, and define
$$\begin{aligned}
E_i^{\mathrm{bot}}
   &=\{z:(R_i+2,z)\in T(H_i)\},\\
E_{i+1}^{\mathrm{top}}

\end{aligned}$$
The original placement needs
$$E_i^{\mathrm{bot}}\cap E_{i+1}^{\mathrm{top}}=\varnothing
\qquad(0\le i<p-1).
\tag{*}$$
This is the only distinct- $H$  interface where endpoint distance three can occur. The arm separations and the other chamber separations are sufficient.Opposite column parities for these facing support sets would prove  $(*)$ . Empty facing support sets could also settle it.
